2026-12-19.title: 19 December · Advent Weekday (O Root of Jesse)
readings: The birth of Samson is announced
My mouth shall be filled with your praise, and I will sing your glory!
The birth of John the Baptist is announced
2026-12-19.alt: O Antiphon: O Radix Jesse (O Root of Jesse).
2026-12-19.verse: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.”
theo: Today's O Antiphon: “O Root of Jesse, who stand as a sign for the peoples, before whom kings shall keep silence and whom the nations shall seek: come and deliver us, and delay no longer” (cf. Isaiah 11:10). Two barren couples receive good news. An angel tells Manoah's wife she will bear a son, Samson, a nazirite consecrated to God from the womb. In the Temple, the angel Gabriel tells the old priest Zechariah that Elizabeth will bear a son, John, “filled with the Holy Spirit” even before his birth, who will go before the Lord “with the spirit and power of Elijah”.

Zechariah doubts and becomes mute until the promise is fulfilled. His silence is not only punishment; it is a time of waiting, of interior listening, that will burst into the Benedictus at John's birth. Elizabeth rejoices: “This is what the Lord has done for me… he looked favourably on me and took away the disgrace I have endured.” In the last days of Advent, God turns barrenness into life, silence into song.
outline: Ask: what in your life feels barren?
God gives life where none seemed possible.
Samson and John belong to God from the start.
live: Spend fifteen minutes in silence today, without phone or noise.
Pray for couples longing for children, and for all who wait.
2026-12-19.prayer: O Root of Jesse, sign for the peoples, come and deliver us, and delay no longer. Hear my long prayers as you heard Zechariah's, turn my barren places into life, and turn my silence into praise. Amen.
altar: At Mass, in the sanctuary like Zechariah, we offer our prayers. God hears, and gives himself in answer.

quick: John is filled with the Spirit from the womb.
2026-12-19.action: Spend fifteen minutes in silence today.
2026-12-19.question: Do I believe God has heard my long prayers?

family.explain: Zechariah prayed for a baby for many years. When the angel said yes, he could not believe it. God always hears our prayers.
family.intention: We pray for couples who are waiting for a child.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we praying for, and do we believe God hears us?”

pm.open: O Root of Jesse, sign for the peoples, come to deliver us and delay no longer. Lord, as we gather, renew our faith that you hear our prayers. Amen.
share: Zechariah prayed for years, then doubted the answer (Luke 1:18). Do I really expect God to answer me?
Elizabeth said: this is what the Lord has done for me (Luke 1:25). What has God done for me this year?
What prayer have I almost given up on?
interc: For the Church, that she may pray with faith and expectation.
For couples longing for a child.
For those whose prayers seem unanswered, that they may not lose heart.
For the elderly, that they may still find hope in God's promises.
For our group, that we may believe and give thanks.
pm.close: Lord God, you heard the prayer of Zechariah and Elizabeth. Strengthen our faith, and help us trust your timing as we wait for the coming of your Son. Amen.

illus: A couple in Changanacherry prayed for a child for fourteen years. When the doctor finally said the wife was pregnant, the husband laughed: “I had stopped believing.” They named their daughter Elizabeth.

homily: Dear friends, today's O Antiphon prays: O Root of Jesse, standing as a sign for the peoples, before whom kings shall keep silent: come to deliver us and delay no longer.

In the first reading the wife of Manoah is barren. An angel appears and tells her she will bear a son, Samson, who will be a Nazirite, consecrated to God from birth, and he will begin to save Israel (Judges 13:2–5). God brings life where there was none.

In the Gospel the angel Gabriel appears to the old priest Zechariah in the Temple: your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John. He will turn many of the people of Israel to the Lord their God (Luke 1:13–16).
But Zechariah doubts: how will I know that this is so? For I am an old man, and my wife is getting on in years (Luke 1:18). Because he did not believe, he becomes mute until the child is born.

Zechariah had prayed for years. When the answer finally came, he could not believe it. How often we pray without really expecting God to answer! Elizabeth, on the other hand, says: this is what the Lord has done for me; he has taken away my disgrace (Luke 1:25).

As Christmas draws near, let us renew our faith in prayer. God hears. His timing is not ours, but he hears. Let us keep praying for what we long for, and when God answers, in his way, let us believe and give thanks. Amen.
kids: Children, Zechariah prayed for a long time, and God answered. Keep praying, even if the answer takes time!

intro: God turns barrenness into life, consecrates from the womb, and turns silence into song.

sub: God gives life where none seemed possible.
q: And the angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, “Although you are barren, having borne no children, you shall conceive and bear a son.”
But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.”
points.apply: Pray for couples longing for children.

sub: John, filled with the Spirit before birth.
Every life belongs to God from conception.
q: For you shall conceive and bear a son. No razor is to come on his head, for the boy shall be a nazirite to God from birth. It is he who shall begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines.
For he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He must never drink wine or strong drink; even before his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Pray for the protection of unborn life.

q: For you, O Lord, are my hope, my trust, O LORD, from my youth. Upon you I have leaned from my birth; it was you who took me from my mother's womb. My praise is continually of you.
This is what the Lord has done for me when he looked favorably on me and took away the disgrace I have endured among my people.
points.apply: Keep fifteen minutes of silence today.

concl: In silence we prepare our song for Christmas.
2026-12-19.resolve: Make a silent half-hour before the crib on Christmas Eve.
